newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger says conscious of exporters' pain.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger says conscious of exporters' pain.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Tuesday he was conscious that exporters were being punished by the high New Zealand dollar but it was a moot point whether the currency was too high.
Bolger acknowledged that manufacturers and farmers were arguing for tighter control of government spending to curb the currency.
"I'm sure cabinet will take that into account today when we start to do very, very preliminary discussions on this year's budget," he told Radio New Zealand.

Bolger said: "We're conscious that the exporters are being punished by a very high dollar. We're equally conscious that the economy is going strongly, the sharemarket's at its highest level, interest rates have come down, the level of optimism's still very high out there.
"So we've got a strong economy, or a stronger economy, creating interest in the New Zealand dollar and that is keeping the New Zealand dollar high."

Asked if the currency was too high, Bolger said that was a moot point. Its value would finally be determined by the market, which perceived that New Zealand had improved its economic performance dramatically over recent years.
He said intervention to set the level of the currency had failed New Zealand in the past.
"I don't think the Reserve Bank can intervene in a way that's going to just bring the dollar down," Bolger said.
